name: Macular Coloboma-Cleft Palate-Hallux Valgus Syndrome
aliases: Macular Coloboma with Cleft Palate and Hallux Valgus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Macular Coloboma-Cleft Palate-Hallux Valgus Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of macular coloboma confirmed by ophthalmological examination
Congenital cleft palate identified clinically or surgically
Hallux valgus deformity of the foot confirmed by clinical or radiological assessment
Characteristic facial features including broad nasal bridge and micrognathia
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: macular coloboma, cleft palate, and hallux valgus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive due to limited data.

pathognomonic.notes: Distinctive congenital defect of the macula leading to visual impairment
Midline defect of the palate causing feeding and speech difficulties
Lateral deviation of the great toe with medial prominence of the first metatarsal head

common.notes: Small lower jaw contributing to feeding and airway issues
Variable degree of vision loss related to macular coloboma
Secondary to cleft palate and associated velopharyngeal insufficiency

occasional.notes: Due to cleft palate and associated oral dysfunction
Reported in some cases, etiology unclear
Secondary to middle ear effusions or structural anomalies
searchTerms: hearing loss due to ear conduction issues

occasional.notes: Partial webbing of toes occasionally observed

searchTerms: holes or defects in heart walls

rare.notes: Mild muscle tone reduction reported rarely

imaging: Radiographs of feet confirming hallux valgus deformity
Palatal imaging or endoscopy confirming cleft palate
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Genetic testing currently non-diagnostic but may exclude other syndromes
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic facial dysmorphism

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of iris coloboma rather than macular coloboma
Characteristic anal atresia and preauricular tags
Cleft lip and/or palate with lower lip pits

redFlags: Severe visual impairment from macular coloboma
Feeding difficulties causing failure to thrive due to cleft palate
references: Orphanet: Macular Coloboma-Cleft Palate-Hallux Valgus Syndrome (ORPHA:91494)
